messages:
claire: Quick sketch: sparse-prefetch handoff latency mitigation. Problem: hot prefixes spilled between slabs cause bursts of full-lease handoffs that spike latency. Idea: introduce a tiny "handoff-window token" cached alongside prefix projection so handoffs within window are treated as "soft-handoff" and avoid heavy sequencer consults.

yusuf: Soft-handoff = best-effort lease transfer that can be retried/validated later? risk: lost ownership if node crashes during soft-handoff.

claire: Correct. Safety model: soft-handoff can be used for eviction/admit decisions and short-lived reads. Any write or durable handback must still consult full lease. On crash/restart we revalidate against sequencer; soft-handoff never changes canonical ownership.

dan: How do we bound false positives (soft-handoff used when it shouldn't)?

claire: We attach a short TTL (default 30s) and require monotonic session id so we can detect ABA. If we observe mismatch during stitch we revert and bump a tenant-specific cooldown. Also track soft_handoff_fallback_rate metric.

yusuf: What about churned small tenants? They might thrash soft-handoff repeatedly. Suggest tenant-weighted grace and an adaptive TTL that shrinks with churn signal.

claire: Agreed. Adaptive TTL: base 30s, halved for high-churn tenants, doubled for low-churn. Plan metrics: soft_handoff_hit_rate, fallback_rate, evict_latency_percentiles, stall_detect_rate. Canary gate: fallback_rate < 0.1% and no p99 eviction latency regressions.

dan: Rollout: feature-flag soft-handoff, start read-only telemetry, then canary on specific slab pool. Need emergency flip to force full-lease consults. Also add daily sampler comparing 100 random handoffs decisions with and without soft-handoff.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag soft-handoff canary=7% cluster="prefetch-pool-1" (requested by claire).

claire: Next steps: write RFC with interface + safety proof sketch, prototype branch `handoff/soft-window`, add dashboards and chaos test (node crash during soft-handoff). Booking 20m sync Tue 11am to review. Thanks :thumbsup:
